groups.text:
For each question from 16 to 20, choose the word(s) closest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

Aziz, Bala and Cooper were bubbling with excitement. They __(16: scurried)__ about the kitchen preparing for their picnic. Sunlight streamed through the windows as they packed sandwiches, __(17: juicy)__ slices of watermelon and a flask of chilled lemonade into a __(18: sturdy)__ woven basket.
Aziz made sure to put the first aid kit that they had prepared earlier into the basket as well. "__(19: It is good to be prepared)__!" he said with a grin.
Bala and Cooper replied in unison, "You're right!" He then checked the contents __(20: thoroughly)__ before shutting it. With unwavering enthusiasm, they ensured that everything was perfect. Finally, they were ready for the picnic.

Study the information for an event (Text 1) and the extract from a school newsletter (Text 2) and answer questions 21 to 25.

++Text 1++
The text below provides information for an event.
[[img1]]
++Text 2++
The extract below, from a school newsletter, is a student's journal entry about the upcoming school park run.
The school park run is not just about running. Whether you are a talented runner or just simply a beginner, it is about coming together as a school community to stay active and have fun. When we all join in, regardless of your running speed, we learn to support one another. Even when it is tough, we keep going because we know our friends are there to cheer us on. It is not about winning. It is about motivating oneself to complete the entire course from start to end and having a sense of achievement as a result.
Running with our classmates makes us feel like we are a part of one big family. We show determination, encourage one another and feel a sense of pride as a member of the school. Moreover, it is a great way to keep fit. With each step, we are building our endurance and growing stronger, both physically and mentally!
So, let's hit the trail and embrace the adventure of the school park run! Together, we will run, laugh and make memories that will last a lifetime!

images.alt: Event information sheet. Heading: Sunshine Primary School 5th Annual Park Run. Ready to run, bond and build lasting memories? Date: 3 September 2026. Reporting time: 8.15 a.m. In a starburst: Primary 3 to 6 students. Bullet points: To promote physical well-being. To foster school community spirit. Assemble at the hall for attendance-taking. Primary 1 and 2 will remain in school to participate in the Sports Carnival. Below is a map headed PARK RUN ROUTE AT CREST PARK. It shows one looping track. START LINE (Primary 4-6) is at the bottom of the loop. START LINE (Primary 3) is further along the track, on the right side. The track then passes Checkpoint 1 (top right), Checkpoint 2 (top middle) and Checkpoint 3 (top left) and ends at one FINISHING LINE at the bottom left. Distances: Primary 3: 1 km. Primary 4-6: 1.6 km. Note: 2 teachers will be stationed at each checkpoint with a first aid kit. A water point is available at Checkpoint 2.

There are 10 blanks, numbered 26 to 35, in the passage below. From the list of words given, choose the most suitable word for each blank. Write its letter (A to Q) in the blank. The letters (I) and (O) have been omitted to avoid confusion during marking.
**EACH WORD CAN BE USED ONLY ONCE.**
[[table1]]

Have you heard of the Purple Parade? Every year, this event brings people together to celebrate the inclusivity __(26)__ individuals with special needs. By wearing purple to the event, it is hoped that national awareness of the needs of these people __(27)__ be raised.
Purple is a great choice of colour – it has __(28)__ been considered the colour of royalty. In fact, not __(29)__ could wear purple! It was reserved for the upper class in the past. Some Roman emperors even forbade __(30)__ people from wearing it. Purple dye in __(31)__ days came from tiny sea snails and was extremely rare. __(32)__ was therefore extremely expensive. Purple was worn not only to show wealth __(33)__ also to signal authority, prestige and power. The Persian king, Cyrus, was known for wearing __(34)__ purple robe for royal ceremonies.
Purple, a blend of rich red and blue colours, __(35)__ everywhere in royal life back then. Rulers wore purple robes and signed letters with purple ink. Royal children were described as being "born in the purple".
Don't you think that the colour purple has such a rich history?

Each of the underlined words contains either a spelling or grammatical error. Write the correct word in each of the boxes.

Last month, my family and I went camping at Corine Beach. Initially, I was not excited about the trip as I had __(36: prefer)__ staying indoors reading to spending time outdoors. Camping sounded __(37: unkumftible)__, especially since we had to sleep in a tent without any air conditioning.
However, my perspective changed __(38: drastiquely)__ on the first evening. As the sun began to set, the sky was painted in shades of orange and pink. Always __(39: imerssed)__ in my books, I hardly paid attention to sunsets until that day. The __(40: glory)__ masterpiece was a sight to behold. That night, the __(41: soothe)__ sound of the waves gently crashing against the shore lulled me __(42: in)__ sleep.
The next morning, I __(43: awake)__, feeling refreshed. Exploring the area, we were greeted by a __(44: plithora)__ of colourful flowers, birds, and insects. My mother and I spent hours on the beach, collecting interesting shells and watching crabs scuttle across the sand. My father introduced to me the different plants and I learnt that each one plays a __(45: krushial)__ role in the ecosystem. That camping trip was truly amazing.

Fill in each blank with a suitable word.

What do you usually eat during recess? School meals around the world __(46)__ greatly. However, they all share a common goal – to nourish young minds and bodies. In France, school lunches are served in several parts. The meal __(47)__ with an appetiser, followed by a main dish __(48)__ of protein like salmon or lamb. Next, students enjoy their cheese and bread. Finally, they wrap up the meal with dessert. These provide students with an __(49)__ of vitamins and minerals.
Japan takes a unique approach to school dining. Nearly all primary school lunches use only locally grown, fresh __(50)__ – vegetables, fruits and mushrooms – obtained from nearby farms. School lunch menus are usually __(51)__ up by a nutritionist.
Singapore's school canteens offer the most diverse dining __(52)__, reflecting the nation's multicultural heritage. Students can choose __(53)__ various stalls selling Chinese, Indian, Malay, and Western food. The Healthy Meals in Schools Programme has been implemented to __(54)__ students on making healthier food and beverage choices. As __(55)__ of this initiative, canteen vendors are required to serve wholegrains, fruits, and vegetables daily. Therefore, they __(56)__ mandatory training by the Health Promotion Board. Routine checks by schools are conducted to ensure that they __(57)__ with nutrition guidelines.
This programme ensures that students obtain appropriate nutrients for their growing needs. Snacks sold have to come __(58)__ the Healthier Choice symbol. Plain water is the ideal beverage choice while drinks artificially __(59)__ by sugar are strongly discouraged. Likewise, processed foods are also not recommended. They are often high in salt, which __(60)__ the risk of heart disease. Through these efforts, Singapore's schools are helping students develop lifelong healthy eating habits that will benefit them well into adulthood.

Read the passage and answer questions 66 to 75.

**1** Colin's school holidays in the city had always been busy and exciting. If he was not out with his friends, the twelve-year-old would be playing computer games in the comfort of his air-conditioned bedroom. Thus, when his parents sent him to stay with his grandmother on a countryside farm, Colin expected **a month of boredom**.
**2** The moment Colin stepped onto the dirt path, he wrinkled his nose at the earthy smell clinging to his shoes. The sky seemed wider, the air calmer, and even the sun rose slowly, spilling gold rays across the fields. He spotted a figure bent over, her hands moving busily, plucking out invasive stems that competed with the crops for nutrients and space.
**3** Upon hearing him approach, she straightened up and dusted her hands on her jeans. Then, she greeted him warmly, "Welcome, Colin. It's been a long time since you were here. Today, I'll show you something different. You don't see **this** happening in the city."
**4** **Colin eyed Grandma warily**. What was she going to show him? How special could something on the farm be? Colin followed his grandmother to the chicken coop, dragging his feet as he walked. There, hens clucked loudly, jostling for the grains scattered across the ground. Suddenly, one large hen shoved the others aside, pecking greedily while the smaller birds waited in quiet submission. Colin grimaced. Why did they let it push them around?
**5** Grandma patted Colin on the shoulder gently. "What's with the frown?" she asked, pointing at the chickens. "See what they are doing? They know how to get food despite being smaller!" Colin watched more closely and noticed the smaller hens pecking at the grains when the larger one turned away. He started to smile.
**6** By midday, dark clouds gathered. Wind whipped across the farm, rattling fences and tugging at the coop door. With a loud creak, the door swung open. Rain poured down, and the hens burst out in a flurry of feathers and panicked clucks.
**7** "Grandma! The chickens!" Colin shouted, his heart racing. The birds scattered in all directions and showed no sign of turning back – some charged towards the open field while others darted under the bushes. Colin's first instinct was to sprint after them, but they were swifter than he was.
**8** "Wait! They're not as bold as the large one!" Grandma called over the rain. Colin froze. What if they never came back? His chest tightened as he breathed hard and fast. Then he remembered the smaller hens at feeding time – how they had waited, watched, and chosen **the right moment**. Being impulsive would not help.
**9** Taking a deep breath, Colin changed his strategy. He slowed his steps and softened his movements. Instead of chasing, he began guiding. He circled behind two hens, gently steering them towards the coop. He clapped lightly, not to scare them, but to direct them. One by one, a few hens began to return. He inhaled deeply, suppressing a smile. The large one, however, remained in the field, tense and alert. Each time Colin moved too quickly, it darted farther away. Colin muttered in frustration, "Why can't you just come back?" He took another deep breath and stood still for a moment, thinking.
**10** Colin waited with bated breath. For a long moment, **nothing** happened. Then, slowly, the hen tilted its head, noticing the grains that led towards the coop. Step by step, it followed the bait. Colin resisted the urge to rush. At last, the hen crossed into the coop. Colin quickly shut the door. He was drenched and muddy, yet quietly triumphant. Grandma nodded and said, "Getting drenched is totally worth it – nothing teaches you how to wait like the chickens!"

questions.stem: I __________ this movie several times but I still find it enjoyable each time I do.

explanation: Clue: 'several times'. The watching happened a number of times at some point before now, and it still matters now.
Rule: use the present perfect (have + past participle) for actions completed before now when the exact time is not given, especially with 'several times', 'twice', 'before'.
'have been watching' is tempting, but the continuous form is for one activity that is still going on, not for a counted number of finished times.
'I have watched this movie several times...' The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: "__________ among the passengers witnessed the accident and reported it?" the reporter asked the police.

explanation: The blank is the subject of the verbs 'witnessed' and 'reported', and it stands for a person (one of the passengers).
Rule: use 'Who' to ask about a person who does the action. 'Whom' is for the person who receives the action (Whom did you see?).
'Which' is tempting because there is a group to choose from, but it normally comes with a noun or 'of' (Which passenger...? Which of the passengers...?). 'What' is for things.
'Who among the passengers witnessed the accident...?' The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: Neither of the twins __________ sleepy. They are still playing in their room.

explanation: Rule: 'Neither of' + plural noun takes a singular verb, because it means 'not one and not the other'.
That rules out 'are' and 'were'.
Tense clue: the next sentence is in the present ('They are still playing'), so we need the present 'is', not 'was'.
'Neither of the twins is sleepy.' The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: The coach attributed the team's success __________ their consistent effort and dedication.

explanation: Some verbs go with a fixed preposition. We attribute something **to** its cause.
'attribute A to B' means to say that A happened because of B. Example: 'She attributed her good results to hard work.'
'by' is tempting because we think 'caused by', but 'attributed by' is wrong.
'...attributed the team's success to their consistent effort...' The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: Hardly anyone in class knew the answer to this question, __________?

explanation: Rule: a negative statement takes a positive question tag.
'Hardly' means 'almost no', so 'Hardly anyone ... knew' counts as a negative statement, even though there is no 'not'. The tag must be positive, which rules out 'didn't they' and 'hadn't they'.
'knew' is the simple past, so the helping verb in the tag is 'did', not 'had'. 'anyone' becomes 'they' in a tag.
'Hardly anyone in class knew the answer..., did they?' The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: __________ the ongoing construction work at the school field, the football match was postponed.

explanation: Work out how the two halves are linked: the construction work is the reason, and postponing the match is the action taken because of it.
'In response to' means 'as a reaction to'. The match was postponed as a reaction to the construction work.

'In spite of' shows contrast and would fit only if the match had gone on anyway. 'In the event of' means 'if it happens' and is for something that may happen later, but the work is already 'ongoing'. 'In addition to' adds one more thing.
The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: The group's success depends __________ on effective collaboration than individual ability.

explanation: Clue: 'than'. It tells us two things are being compared, so we need a comparative form (more or less), not a superlative (most or least).
Now think about meaning. It is a **group's** success, and collaboration means working together well. A group succeeds mainly through working together.
So the success depends 'more on effective collaboration than individual ability'. 'less' is grammatical but gives the opposite, unlikely meaning.
The answer is option (3).

review.note: The key's digit for Q7 is partly under the watermark; it reads 3, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: The teacher made the class __________ the furniture for the oral examination the next day.

explanation: Rule: make + person + base form of the verb (no 'to', no '-s', no '-ed'). It means to cause or force someone to do something.
Example: 'Mother made me tidy my room.'
'arranged' is tempting because the sentence is in the past, but 'made' already carries the past tense. The second verb stays in its base form.
'The teacher made the class arrange the furniture...' The answer is option (1).

review.note: The key's digit for Q8 is partly under the watermark; it reads 1, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Anna, as well as her classmate, Tom, completed the marble run project by __________.

explanation: Find the real subject. The words between the commas, 'as well as her classmate, Tom,' are only extra information. They do not become part of the subject.
Rule: with 'as well as', 'together with' and 'along with', the subject is the noun before the phrase. Here the subject is 'Anna' alone.
A reflexive pronoun must match the subject. Anna is one girl, so the pronoun is 'herself'.
'themselves' is tempting because two people are named, but it would be right only with 'Anna **and** Tom'. The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: Without __________ equipment, the team still managed to complete the project successfully.

explanation: 'Equipment' is an uncountable noun (we cannot say 'an equipment' or 'equipments'). 'few' and 'many' are for countable plural nouns, so they are out.
That leaves 'little' and 'much'. 'Without much equipment' means 'not having a lot of equipment'.
'little' already means 'almost none', so 'without little' does not make sense.
'still managed' shows they succeeded even though they did not have much. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Hui Ling had to deal with the __________ of repeatedly submitting homework after the deadline.

explanation: Clue: she handed in homework late again and again, and then 'had to deal with' what followed. We need a word for an unpleasant result of an action.
'repercussion' means an unwelcome consequence of something you did.
'retaliation' is hurting someone back in revenge, and 'deterrence' is stopping people from doing something by making them fear the result. 'damage' is physical harm.
The answer is option (4), repercussion.

questions.stem: Artificial intelligence will be introduced to schools __________ to give students time to adapt to it.

explanation: Clue: 'to give students time to adapt'. The change must come slowly, step by step.
'progressively' means gradually, in stages.
'intermittently' is tempting, but it means stopping and starting at irregular times, not moving steadily forward. 'incessantly' means without stopping, and 'simultaneously' means at the same time.
The answer is option (3), progressively.

questions.stem: The volcanic eruption __________ the flight schedules in the region due to poor visibility.

explanation: We need a word for what the eruption did to 'flight schedules', which are plans and timetables.
'disrupted' means stopped something from carrying on in its normal way. Schedules, services and lessons are disrupted.

'diverted' is tempting because flights can be diverted (sent to another airport), but a schedule cannot be sent somewhere else. 'disturbed' is used for people, sleep or peace, and 'disabled' for machines.
The answer is option (3), disrupted.

questions.stem: The doctor advised him not to __________ his persistent headaches as they might have a detrimental effect on his health.

explanation: Clue: the headaches 'might have a detrimental (harmful) effect', so the doctor wants him to take them seriously.
'brush off' means to refuse to pay attention to something, treating it as unimportant. The doctor advised him not to do that.
'wear off' is tempting because pain can wear off (slowly go away), but a person cannot 'wear off' a headache. 'call off' means cancel and 'hold off' means delay.
The answer is option (4), brush off.

questions.stem: Ever so __________, Mohan presented complex ideas in a way that was easy to understand.

explanation: Clue: his ideas were complex, yet 'easy to understand'. We need a word for someone who expresses ideas clearly. ('Ever so' means 'very'.)
'coherent' means clear, logical and easy to follow.
'consistent' is tempting because it looks similar, but it means always behaving in the same way. 'objective' means not influenced by personal feelings, and 'dexterous' means skilful with the hands.
The answer is option (1), coherent.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++scurried++.

explanation: To 'scurry' is to move quickly with short, hurried steps.
Clue: the boys were 'bubbling with excitement' and busy preparing, so they were moving about quickly.
'scampered' also means ran with quick, light steps, so it is the closest.
'wandered' means walked slowly with no purpose, and 'prowled' means moved quietly as if hunting. 'fussed' is about worrying over small things, not about moving. The answer is option (4).

review.note: The key's digit for Q16 is partly under the watermark; the visible strokes are a 4, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++juicy++.

explanation: 'juicy' means full of juice.
'succulent' means juicy and tender, so it is the closest.
'delectable' and 'palatable' are tempting because the watermelon would be nice to eat, but they are about a pleasant taste, not about being full of juice.
'savoury' means salty or spicy rather than sweet. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++sturdy++.

explanation: 'sturdy' means strong and not easily broken. The basket had to hold sandwiches, watermelon, a flask and a first aid kit.
'robust' means strong and solid, so it is the closest.
'malleable' is nearly the opposite: easy to bend or press into a new shape. 'intricate' means having many small details, and 'versatile' means having many uses.
The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: Choose the words closest in meaning to ++It is good to be prepared++.

explanation: Aziz said this as he packed a first aid kit, in case someone got hurt at the picnic. He was taking care in advance.
'Better safe than sorry' means it is wiser to be careful and take precautions than to regret it later. That matches.
'Save for a rainy day' is tempting, but it is about keeping money for a time of need. 'Look before you leap' means think about the results before you act.
'Think on your feet' means to react quickly without preparing. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++thoroughly++.

explanation: 'thoroughly' means completely and with great attention to detail. Clue: 'they ensured that everything was perfect'.
'painstakingly' means with great care and effort, checking every detail, so it is the closest.
'extensively' is tempting, but it means over a wide area or range (he travelled extensively), not carefully. 'deliberately' means on purpose or slowly.
'gingerly' means in a careful, nervous way so as not to break or hurt something. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: "Ready to run, bond and build lasting memories?" The purpose of this question in Text 1 is to __________.
options: invite students to join the run
excite students ahead of the run
make students curious about the run

explanation: Look at the words used: 'run, bond and build lasting memories'. They are all fun, happy things to look forward to. A question like this, put to the reader in large bold print, is there to stir up feelings.
So its purpose is to make students excited before the event.
(1) is tempting, but the students are not being invited. The run is for all 'Primary 3 to 6 students', who 'assemble at the hall for attendance-taking', so they are expected to take part.
(2) is the job of the details below it (date, time, route). (4) does not fit because nothing is kept secret. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem:
According to the event information in Text 1, which of the following are true of the run?
A. The reporting venue is Crest Park.
B. All students will have the same end point.
C. There is only one spot to get drinking water.
D. Students can attend the Sports Carnival after the run.

explanation: Check each statement against Text 1.
A is false: students 'Assemble at the hall for attendance-taking'. Crest Park is where the route is, not where they report.
B is true: there are two start lines but only one FINISHING LINE on the map. C is true: the note says 'A water point is available at Checkpoint 2', and no other water point is mentioned.
D is not supported: the Sports Carnival is for Primary 1 and 2, who 'remain in school'. So B and C are true. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Text 1 is most probably __________.

explanation: Look at the layout: a big heading, a catchy line, a starburst, short points for date and time, a map and a note. That is how a poster about an event looks.
It is not a letter: there is no greeting, no paragraphs and no sign-off.
It is not a report: a report is written after an event, but this run is on a coming date.
'a programme itinerary' is tempting, but an itinerary lists activities with their times in order, and here only the reporting time is given. The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: What is the **main** message of Text 2?
options: The school park run showcases talents and fosters empathy.
The school park run builds resilience and deepens relationship.
The school park run promotes active living and a competitive spirit.
The school park run encourages students to be driven and adventurous.

explanation: Both halves of an option must be right. Look for the ideas the writer repeats.
Resilience (not giving up): 'Even when it is tough, we keep going', 'We show determination', 'growing stronger, both physically and mentally'.
Relationships: 'we learn to support one another', 'our friends are there to cheer us on', 'we are a part of one big family'. So (2) matches.

(3) is tempting because of 'stay active' and 'keep fit', but 'It is not about winning' rules out a competitive spirit. (1) fails because the run is for talented runners and beginners alike. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Which idea is expressed in Text 2 but not Text 1?
options: The run promotes a healthy lifestyle.
The run brings the school community together.
The run helps students to create lifelong memories.
The run prepares students to become mentally stronger.

explanation: Cross out every idea that Text 1 also has.
(1) is in Text 1: 'To promote physical well-being'. (2) is in Text 1: 'To foster school community spirit'. (3) is in Text 1: 'build lasting memories'.
Only Text 2 talks about the mind: 'growing stronger, both physically and **mentally**'. Text 1 mentions only physical well-being.
The answer is option (4).

review.note: The key's digit for Q25 is partly under the watermark; it reads 4, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (26). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank joins two nouns: 'the inclusivity ___ individuals with special needs'.
'of' links a noun to the people it is about, like 'the safety of children' or 'the inclusion of everyone'.
The answer is (J) of.

review.note: The key's letter for Q26 is beside the watermark and reads J.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (27). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: After the blank comes 'be raised'. Only a helping verb such as will, can or may can stand before 'be'.
'it is hoped that' looks ahead to something people want to happen in the future, so we use 'will'.
'...awareness of the needs of these people will be raised.' The answer is (Q) will.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (28). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'it has ___ been considered' is already complete (has + been + considered), so the blank needs an adverb that sits between 'has' and 'been'.
'always' is the only adverb in the list. It tells us purple has been linked with royalty for all of history.
The answer is (C) always.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (29). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'not ___ could wear purple!' The next sentence explains: 'It was reserved for the upper class'. So some people could wear it, but not everyone.
'not all' means 'not everyone'.
'any' is tempting, but 'not any could wear' is not correct English, and it would mean nobody could wear purple.
The answer is (B) all.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (30). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank comes before the noun 'people', so we need a word that shows whose people they were.
The people belonged to 'Some Roman emperors' (plural), so the word is 'their'.
'these' and 'those' are tempting because they also go before plural nouns, but no people have been pointed out yet. The emperors forbade their own people.
The answer is (K) their.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (31). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'in ___ days' is a set phrase about time.
'in those days' means at that time in the far past. 'those' points to things far away in time or place.
'these days' means nowadays, but the verb 'came' is in the past and the passage is describing ancient times.
The answer is (M) those.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (32). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank is the subject of 'was therefore extremely expensive', and it starts a new sentence.
What was expensive? The purple dye from the sentence before. One thing is replaced by the pronoun 'It'.
'its' is tempting, but 'its' shows belonging and must be followed by a noun (its colour).
The answer is (G) it.

review.note: The key's letter for Q32 is partly under the watermark; the visible strokes are a G, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (33). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: Look for the partner words: 'not only to show wealth ___ also to signal authority'.
The pair is 'not only ... but also'. It joins two reasons of the same kind.
The answer is (E) but.

review.note: The key's letter for Q33 is partly under the watermark and reads E.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (34). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'wearing ___ purple robe': 'robe' is a singular countable noun, so it needs an article or a similar word in front.
It is one robe, mentioned for the first time, and 'purple' begins with a consonant sound, so we use 'a'.
'its' does not fit because Cyrus is a person (it would have to be 'his').
The answer is (A) a.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (35). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The sentence has no verb yet: 'Purple, ..., ___ everywhere in royal life back then.'
Find the subject by leaving out the words between the commas. The subject is 'Purple', which is singular. 'back then' shows the past. So the verb is 'was'.
'were' is tempting because 'colours' comes just before the blank, but 'a blend of rich red and blue colours' is only extra information about purple.
The answer is (N) was.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (36) ++prefer++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. Look at the helping verb in front: 'I **had** ___ staying indoors'.
Rule: had + past participle makes the past perfect tense, for something that was true before another past time (before the camping trip).
The past participle of 'prefer' is 'preferred'. Double the 'r' because the stress is on the last syllable: pre-FER.
The correct word is 'preferred'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (37) ++unkumftible++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means not feeling pleasant or relaxed, which fits sleeping in a tent without air conditioning.
Build it from parts: un + comfort + able. The base word is 'comfort', spelt with a 'c' and an 'o'.
The ending is '-able', not '-ible'.
The correct word is 'uncomfortable'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (38) ++drastiquely++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means in a sudden and very big way.
It comes from the adjective 'drastic'. Adjectives ending in '-ic' add '-ally' to become adverbs: basic, basically; dramatic, dramatically.
The 'k' sound is spelt 'c', not 'qu'.
The correct word is 'drastically'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (39) ++imerssed++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. To be 'immersed' in books is to be so deeply interested in them that you notice nothing else.
The word has a double 'm' and a single 's': im + mersed.
A related word is 'immersion'.
The correct word is 'immersed'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (40) ++glory++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (wrong word form). 'glory' is a noun.
The blank describes the noun 'masterpiece', so we need an adjective.
Change the 'y' to 'i' and add '-ous': glory, glorious (like fury, furious).
The correct word is 'glorious'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (41) ++soothe++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (wrong word form). 'soothe' is a verb meaning to make someone calm.
The blank describes the noun 'sound', so we need an adjective. A sound that calms you is a 'soothing' sound.
Drop the 'e' before adding '-ing': soothe, soothing.
The correct word is 'soothing'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (42) ++in++.

explanation: This is a grammar error: the wrong preposition.
The set phrase is 'lull someone **to** sleep', meaning to make someone fall asleep gently. 'in sleep' does not show the change from being awake to being asleep.
'lulled me into sleep' is also used and shows the same change.
The correct word is 'to'.

review.note: The key gives only 'to'. 'into' ('lulled me into sleep') is also correct English and is accepted.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (43) ++awake++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (wrong tense). 'The next morning' in this story is in the past, and the other verbs are in the past (went, changed, lulled).
'awake' is an irregular verb: awake, awoke, awoken.
The simple past is 'awoke'.
The correct word is 'awoke'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (44) ++plithora++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. A 'plethora' of something is a very large amount or variety of it.
The first syllable is spelt with an 'e': ple-tho-ra.
The correct word is 'plethora'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (45) ++krushial++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means extremely important.
It begins with a 'c', and the 'shul' sound at the end is spelt '-cial', as in special, social and official.
The correct word is 'crucial'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (46) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence needs a verb: 'School meals around the world ___ greatly.'
The next sentence starts with 'However, they all share a common goal', so this sentence must say the meals are not the same.
'vary' and 'differ' both mean 'are different from one another'. The subject 'meals' is plural, so there is no 's' on the verb.
The answer is 'vary' (or 'differ').

questions.stem: Fill in blank (47) with a suitable word.

explanation: Clues: 'with an appetiser, followed by a main dish ... Next ... Finally'. The meal is described in order, and an appetiser is the first course.
So the meal 'starts with' an appetiser. 'begins' means the same.
'The meal' is singular and the passage is in the present tense, so the verb needs an 's'.
The answer is 'starts'.

review.note: The key gives only 'starts'. 'begins' and 'commences' mean the same and are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (48) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'a main dish ___ of protein like salmon or lamb': the blank is followed by 'of' and tells us what the dish is made up of.
'consist of' means 'be made up of'. After the noun 'dish' we use the -ing form: a main dish consisting of protein.
The answer is 'consisting'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (49) with a suitable word.

explanation: Clue: 'an' tells us the word begins with a vowel sound, and it is followed by 'of vitamins and minerals'.
The meal has many parts (appetiser, main dish, cheese, bread, dessert), so it gives many kinds and plenty of nutrients.
'an array of' means a wide range of. 'an abundance of' means plenty of.
The answer is 'array' (or 'abundance').

questions.stem: Fill in blank (50) with a suitable word.

explanation: Clues: 'locally grown, fresh ___ – vegetables, fruits and mushrooms – obtained from nearby farms'. The words between the dashes are examples of the missing word.
'produce' (a noun) means food that is grown on farms, such as fruit and vegetables.
'ingredients' also fits, because the lunches 'use' these things to make the meals.
The answer is 'produce'.

review.note: The key gives only 'produce'. 'ingredients' also fits the sentence and is accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (51) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank is followed by 'up': 'menus are usually ___ up by a nutritionist'.
The phrasal verb 'draw up' means to prepare and write out a plan or a list.
The sentence is passive (are + past participle), so we need the past participle of 'draw', which is 'drawn'.
The answer is 'drawn'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (52) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'offer the most diverse dining ___': we need a noun for what canteens offer to students who eat there.
Clue: 'diverse' means with a lot of variety, and the next sentence lists Chinese, Indian, Malay and Western food.
A 'dining experience' is the whole experience of eating at a place. 'dining options' or 'choices' also fit, since students choose from many stalls.
The answer is 'experience'.

review.note: The key gives only 'experience'. 'experiences', 'options' and 'choices' also fit the sentence and are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (53) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Students can choose ___ various stalls': the verb 'choose' takes the preposition 'from' when a range of things is given.
Example: 'You can choose from three flavours.'
The answer is 'from'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (54) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'implemented to ___ students on making healthier food and beverage choices': we need a base verb (after 'to') that goes with 'students on'.
A school programme teaches. To 'educate someone on' a topic is to teach them about it.
'teach' does not fit well because we say 'teach students **about**' or 'teach students **to**', not 'teach students on'.
The answer is 'educate'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (55) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'As ___ of this initiative' is a set phrase.
'As part of' means 'as one piece of a bigger plan'. Serving wholegrains, fruits and vegetables is one piece of the programme.
The answer is 'part'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (56) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'they ___ mandatory training': 'they' are the canteen vendors, and 'mandatory' means they must do it.
To 'undergo training' is to go through it. This is the usual word for training, treatment or a test that someone has to go through.
'they' is plural and the passage is in the present tense, so there is no 's' on the verb.
The answer is 'undergo'.

review.note: The key gives only 'undergo'. 'attend' and 'receive' also fit the sentence and are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (57) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'to ensure that they ___ with nutrition guidelines': the blank is followed by 'with', and guidelines are rules to follow.
To 'comply with' rules means to obey them.
'follow' is tempting, but it is not used with 'with' (we say 'follow the guidelines').
The answer is 'comply'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (58) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Snacks sold have to come ___ the Healthier Choice symbol.'
'come with' means to have something attached or included. The snacks must have the symbol on them.
The answer is 'with'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (59) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'drinks artificially ___ by sugar are strongly discouraged': the drinks are compared with 'plain water', and the clue is 'sugar'.
Sugar is added to change the taste of a drink. 'flavoured' means given a taste, and 'sweetened' means made sweet.
We need a past participle (-ed) because something is done to the drinks.
The answer is 'flavoured' (or 'sweetened').

review.note: The key gives 'flavoured'. The solved answer 'sweetened' is the more usual word with 'by sugar' and is accepted as well.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (60) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'They are often high in salt, which ___ the risk of heart disease.' Too much salt is bad for the heart, so it makes the risk greater.
'increases' means makes bigger. 'raises' means the same here.
'which' stands for 'salt' (or for being high in salt), which is singular, and the passage is in the present tense, so the verb needs an 's'.
The answer is 'increases'.

questions.stem:
These towers are not connected by bridges.
None of ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: None of these towers are connected by bridges.
accept: None of these towers is connected by bridges.

explanation: 'None of' means 'not one of' and already carries the negative meaning, so drop 'not'. Writing 'None of these towers are not connected' would be a double negative and change the meaning.
Keep the rest of the sentence the same: 'these towers' follows 'None of', then the verb and 'connected by bridges'.
Keep the present tense. With 'none of' + a plural noun, 'are' is commonly used and 'is' is also accepted.
Answer: None of these towers are connected by bridges.

review.keyAnswer: None of these towers are connected by bridges.
review.solvedAnswer: None of these towers are connected by bridges.
review.note: The full stop after 'bridges' in the given sentence is missing in the scan and has been added.

questions.stem:
The lucky customer chose the last carton of mangoes.
The last ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: The last carton of mangoes was chosen by the lucky customer.

explanation: The new sentence starts with the thing that received the action ('The last carton of mangoes'), so it must be in the passive voice.
Passive voice: object + form of 'to be' + past participle + by + doer.
Tense stays the same: 'chose' is simple past, so use 'was' (the subject 'carton' is singular, even though 'mangoes' is plural). The past participle of 'choose' is 'chosen', not 'chose'.
Answer: The last carton of mangoes was chosen by the lucky customer.

review.keyAnswer: The last carton of mangoes was chose [chosen] by the lucky customer.
review.solvedAnswer: The last carton of mangoes was chosen by the lucky customer.
review.note: The key prints 'was chose', a typing slip for 'was chosen'.

questions.stem:
The girl pronounced the difficult word accurately to impress her teacher.
The girl's accurate ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: The girl's accurate pronunciation of the difficult word impressed her teacher.

explanation: After the possessive 'The girl's' and the adjective 'accurate' we need a noun. Change the verb 'pronounced' into its noun: 'pronunciation'. Watch the spelling: there is no 'o' before the 'u' (not 'pronounciation').
The adverb 'accurately' has already become the adjective 'accurate' in the starter.
Link the noun to its object with 'of': 'pronunciation of the difficult word'.
The noun phrase is now the subject, so finish with a verb: it 'impressed her teacher'. Answer: The girl's accurate pronunciation of the difficult word impressed her teacher.

review.keyAnswer: The girl's accurate pronunciation of the difficult word impressed her teacher.
review.solvedAnswer: The girl's accurate pronunciation of the difficult word impressed her teacher.

questions.stem:
"I won't be joining you for the celebration tomorrow," Vivien told her parents.
Vivien told her parents that ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Vivien told her parents that she would not be joining them for the celebration the next day.
accept: Vivien told her parents that she would not be joining them for the celebration the following day.
Vivien told her parents that she wouldn't be joining them for the celebration the next day.
Vivien told her parents that she wouldn't be joining them for the celebration the following day.

explanation: This is direct speech changed to reported speech. Remove the quotation marks.
Tense moves one step back: 'won't' (will not) becomes 'would not'.
Pronouns change to fit the speaker: 'I' is Vivien, so 'she'; 'you' is her parents, so 'them'.
Time words change: 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' or 'the following day'.
Answer: Vivien told her parents that she would not be joining them for the celebration the next day.

review.keyAnswer: Vivien told her parents that she would not be joining them for the celebration the next day.
review.solvedAnswer: Vivien told her parents that she would not be joining them for the celebration the next day.

questions.stem:
The mountain trail was steep and challenging. The hikers reached the summit successfully.
Undeterred by ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Undeterred by the steep and challenging mountain trail, the hikers reached the summit successfully.
accept: Undeterred by the steep and challenging mountain trail, the hikers successfully reached the summit.
Undeterred by the steep and challenging mountain trail the hikers reached the summit successfully.

explanation: 'Undeterred by' means 'not discouraged by'. It must be followed by a noun phrase, the thing that could have put them off.
Turn the first sentence into a noun phrase by moving the adjectives in front of the noun: 'the steep and challenging mountain trail'. Do not keep 'was'.
Put a comma after the phrase. The very next words must be the people who were undeterred: 'the hikers'.
Keep the rest unchanged. Answer: Undeterred by the steep and challenging mountain trail, the hikers reached the summit successfully.

review.keyAnswer: Undeterred [by] the steep and challenging mountain trail, the hikers reached the summit successful [successfully].
review.solvedAnswer: Undeterred by the steep and challenging mountain trail, the hikers reached the summit successfully.
review.note: The key's sentence has two typing slips: it leaves out 'by' and ends with 'successful'. The model answer corrects both.

questions.stem: In Paragraph 1, Colin went to a countryside farm. Provide two reasons why Colin expected "**a month of boredom**". (line 4, paragraph 1)

parts.label: i

answer.value: He would not be able to play computer games in the comfort of his air-conditioned bedroom.

explanation: Paragraph 1 says what made his city holidays 'busy and exciting': being out with his friends, or 'playing computer games in the comfort of his air-conditioned bedroom'.
On a countryside farm he would have neither of these, so he expected to be bored.
Write each reason as something he would miss on the farm. This reason: he could not play computer games in the comfort of his air-conditioned bedroom.

parts.label: ii
parts.prompt: Second reason: (The two reasons may be given in either order.)

answer.value: He would not be able to go out with his friends.

explanation: The other thing that kept him busy in the city: 'If he was not out with his friends...'.
His friends were in the city, so on the farm he could not go out with them.
The marker looks for two different reasons, one about computer games and one about his friends. Do not split one reason into two.

review.keyAnswer: i) He could not play video games in the comfort of his air conditioned bedroom. ii) He could not go out with his friends.
review.solvedAnswer: He would have no friends to go out with and no computer games in his air-conditioned bedroom. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Circle the word that **best** describes the characters' feelings.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Colin "wrinkled his nose at the earthy smell" (lines 5-6, paragraph 2)
aghast / bored / disgusted
(Type the word you choose.)
explanation: People wrinkle their noses when they find a smell unpleasant. Colin did not like the earthy smell clinging to his shoes.
'disgusted' means feeling strong dislike for something unpleasant.
'aghast' is too strong: it means filled with shock or horror. 'bored' is what he expected to feel later, but it has nothing to do with a smell.
The answer is 'disgusted'.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
"Then, she greeted him warmly" (line 10, paragraph 3)
nostalgic / satisfied / thrilled
(Type the word you choose.)
explanation: Grandma greeted him 'warmly' and said, 'Welcome, Colin. It's been a long time since you were here.' She had not seen him for a long time and was very happy that he had come.
'thrilled' means extremely pleased and excited.
'nostalgic' is tempting because she mentions the past, but it means missing the past with a little sadness. Here she is happy about the present and eager to show him something.
The answer is 'thrilled'.

questions.stem: Explain **in your own words** what Grandma was doing before Colin arrived.

answer.value: She was pulling out weeds from among her crops.

explanation: Find it in paragraph 2: Colin saw 'a figure bent over, her hands moving busily, plucking out invasive stems that competed with the crops for nutrients and space'. The figure was Grandma.
'In your own words' means you must not copy the passage. Change the key words.
'plucking out' can become 'pulling out' or 'removing'. 'invasive stems that competed with the crops for nutrients and space' are weeds (unwanted plants).
The marker looks for: she was pulling out (removing) weeds. Copying 'plucking out invasive stems' gets no mark.

review.solvedAnswer: She was pulling out the weeds growing among the crops. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Why did Colin eye Grandma warily? (line 12, paragraph 4)

answer.value: Colin was not sure what Grandma was going to show him, so he was cautious. He also doubted that anything on a farm could be special.

explanation: 'warily' means in a careful, not trusting way. Look at the two questions in Colin's mind straight after: 'What was she going to show him? How special could something on the farm be?'
Point 1 (1 mark): he did not know what Grandma was going to show him, so he was cautious about it.
Point 2 (1 mark): he was sceptical (doubtful) that anything on a farm could be special or interesting. Remember that he 'expected a month of boredom'.
Turn the two questions into statements. Do not simply copy the questions from the passage.

review.keyAnswer: He was not sure what Grandma was going to show him, so he wanted to be careful. He was sceptical how special something on a farm could be.
review.solvedAnswer: He did not know what she would show him and doubted that anything on a farm could be special. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Which four-word phrase from Paragraph 4 suggests an acceptance of the situation without protest?

explanation: In paragraph 4, the large hen 'shoved the others aside, pecking greedily while the smaller birds waited in quiet submission'.
'submission' means giving in to someone stronger, and 'quiet' shows they did not fight back or make a fuss. That is accepting the situation without protest.
Count exactly four words and copy them without changing anything: waited (1) in (2) quiet (3) submission (4). Writing more or fewer words loses the mark.
The answer is 'waited in quiet submission'.

questions.stem: Based on lines 9-31 (paragraphs 3 to 8), state whether each statement in the table below is true or false, then give one reason why you think so.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Colin had visited Grandma before.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. Grandma said that it had been a long time since Colin was last there, so he had visited the farm before.

explanation: Paragraph 3: Grandma greeted him with 'It's been a long time since you were here.'
'since you were here' tells us he had been to the farm before, a long time ago.
So the statement is True. The reason must be evidence from the passage, not the statement repeated.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Grandma cared about Colin's feelings.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. When Grandma saw Colin grimacing at the smaller hens being pushed around by the large hen, she patted him gently on the shoulder, asked what was wrong and explained what the hens were doing to comfort him.

explanation: Paragraph 4 ends with 'Colin grimaced.' He was upset to see the smaller hens being pushed around.
Paragraph 5: 'Grandma patted Colin on the shoulder gently. "What's with the frown?" she asked', and then she explained that the smaller hens 'know how to get food despite being smaller'.
She noticed how he felt and tried to make him feel better. So the statement is True.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt:
According to Grandma, the smaller hens were easily frightened.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. Grandma called out to Colin that the hens were not as bold as the large one.

explanation: Paragraph 8: when Colin wanted to sprint after the hens that had escaped, Grandma called, 'Wait! They're not as bold as the large one!'
'not as bold' means more timid. She was warning him that these hens scare easily, so chasing them would only drive them further away.
So the statement is True, and the reason is what Grandma said about them.

review.keyAnswer: a) True --- Colin had visited the farm before where Grandma lived a long time ago. b) True --- When Grandma saw Colin grimacing when he saw the smaller hens getting pushed around by the big hen, she patted him on the shoulder and explained what they were doing to comfort him. c) [not given in the key]
review.solvedAnswer: a) True; b) True; c) True (Grandma said they were not as bold as the large one). Agrees with key for (a) and (b).
review.note: The key gives answers for (a) and (b) only; there is no entry for (c). The answer to (c) is the solver's own: True, because Grandma said the hens were 'not as bold as the large one' (line 28). A parent may wish to confirm it with the school's marking. Parts of the key's lines for (a) and (b) are under the watermark but readable.

questions.stem: Explain clearly what had caused the hens to escape.

answer.value: The strong wind tugged at the coop door and made it swing open. When the rain poured down, the hens were frightened and ran out through the open door.

explanation: Find it in paragraph 6: 'Wind whipped across the farm, rattling fences and tugging at the coop door. With a loud creak, the door swung open. Rain poured down, and the hens burst out in a flurry of feathers and panicked clucks.'
'Explain clearly' for 2 marks needs the chain of events, not just one cause.
Point 1 (1 mark): the wind tugged at the coop door until it swung open.
Point 2 (1 mark): the rain poured down and the hens panicked ('panicked clucks'), so they rushed out of the open coop.

review.keyAnswer: It was about to rain and the wind tugged at the coop door, making it swing open. When it started raining the hens were scared and run [ran] out of the open coop.
review.solvedAnswer: The wind pulled the coop door open, and the pouring rain made the hens panic and rush out. Agrees with key.
review.note: The first words of each line of the key's answer are under the watermark but readable.

questions.stem: Look at the table below. What do the word(s) in the left column refer to in the passage? Write your answers in the column on the right.

parts.label: a

answer.value: The hens feeding and fighting over the grains (with the smaller hens still managing to get their food).
accept: the hens feeding and fighting over the grains
the hens feeding and jostling for the grains

explanation: Here 'this' points forward. Grandma says, 'Today, I'll show you something different. You don't see **this** happening in the city.'
Read on to see what she showed him: at the chicken coop, the hens were 'jostling for the grains', the large hen shoved the others aside, and the smaller hens got their food when it turned away.
'this' is something 'happening', so the answer must be an event, not just 'the hens'.
The answer is the hens feeding and jostling (fighting) for the grains.

parts.label: b

answer.value: The moment when the larger hen turned away from the grains.
accept: when the larger hen turned away
when the larger hen turned away from the grains
when the large hen turned away
when the larger one turned away

explanation: Colin 'remembered the smaller hens at feeding time – how they had waited, watched, and chosen **the right moment**'.
Go back to feeding time in paragraph 5: he 'noticed the smaller hens pecking at the grains when the larger one turned away'.
So the right moment for the smaller hens to eat was when the larger hen was not looking.
The answer is when the larger hen turned away (from the grains).

parts.label: c

answer.value: The large hen not moving from the field (it did not come towards the coop).
accept: the larger hen did not move from the field
the large hen did not move from the field
the large hen did not move

explanation: 'For a long moment, **nothing** happened.' Ask: what was Colin waiting for?
At the end of paragraph 9, 'The large one, however, remained in the field, tense and alert', and Colin stood still, waiting.
The next sentence shows what finally happened: 'Then, slowly, the hen tilted its head...'. So before that, the large hen did not move.
The answer is the large hen staying where it was in the field and not moving.

review.keyAnswer: a) The hens feeding and fighting b) When the larger hen turned away from the grains. c) The larger hen did not move from the field.
review.solvedAnswer: a) what the hens were doing at feeding time (jostling for grains, smaller ones still getting food); b) when the larger hen turned away; c) the large hen not moving. Agrees with key.
review.note: The part labels a), b), c) in the key are under the watermark; the three answers are readable.

questions.stem: Explain clearly how Colin lured the large hen back to its coop.

answer.value: Colin spread grains in a trail that led towards the coop as bait, then waited patiently without rushing. The hen noticed the grains and followed them step by step, eating them, until it crossed into the coop.

explanation: To 'lure' is to attract an animal by offering something it wants. Look in paragraph 10 for what attracted the hen.
'the hen tilted its head, noticing the grains that led towards the coop. Step by step, it followed the bait.' 'bait' tells us the grains were put there on purpose to draw the hen in.
Point 1 (1 mark): Colin laid out grains leading towards the coop as bait.
Point 2 (1 mark): the hen noticed the grains and followed them into the coop, while Colin waited and 'resisted the urge to rush'.

review.keyAnswer: Colin spread grains that led towards the coop. The hen noticed the grains left out as bait and ate them going back to the coop.
review.solvedAnswer: He used a trail of grains leading to the coop as bait and waited without rushing; the hen followed it in. Agrees with key.
review.note: The first words of the key's second line are under the watermark; they read 'grains left out as bait'.

questions.stem: Complete the information below.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: One lesson Colin learnt from the visit is ____________________.

accept: to be patient and not impulsive

explanation: Look at Grandma's last words: 'nothing teaches you how to wait like the chickens!' Knowing how to wait is patience.
It also matches what Colin realised in paragraph 8: 'Being impulsive would not help.'
The answer is to be patient (not to act impulsively).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Cite a piece of evidence to support your answer in (a).

answer.value: Instead of being impulsive and sprinting after the hens, Colin guided them slowly. When the large hen followed the bait towards the coop, he resisted the urge to rush so that he would not scare it away.

explanation: The evidence must show Colin being patient, and it must match your answer in (a).
Paragraph 9: 'Instead of chasing, he began guiding.' He slowed his steps and steered the hens gently.
Paragraph 10: 'Colin waited with bated breath' and 'Colin resisted the urge to rush' while the large hen followed the bait step by step.
Either piece of evidence is accepted. Say what Colin did, not only what Grandma said.

review.keyAnswer: a) to be patient b) Instead of being impulsive and sprinting after hens, he guided the hens slowly. The larger hen followed the bait into the coop slowly and Colin resisted the urge not to rush [to rush] in order not to scare it away to bring it back to the coop.
review.solvedAnswer: a) patience; b) he resisted the urge to rush and waited while the hen followed the bait. Agrees with key.
review.note: The key's 'resisted the urge not to rush' is a slip for 'resisted the urge to rush'.

questions.stem:
Part 1: Situational Writing
The pictures below show Vincent, Leah and Siti having a conversation. Study the pictures carefully.
[[img1]]
++Your Task++
Imagine you are Vincent.
**Write an email to your form teacher, Mrs Wong, to propose the ideas for the project you and your classmates have discussed.**
You are to refer to the pictures and information on page 2 (shown above) for your email. The bullet point underlined below requires you to come up with your own information.
In your email, include the following key information:
• the name and objective of the Values-in-Action project
• how the activity was decided
• the items to be purchased and by when you hope to get them
• ++one way the class plans to interact with the elderly++
You may reorder the points. Remember to write in complete sentences.

images.alt: Two cartoon panels set in a school library, dated 17 August 2026. Three pupils are talking: Vincent (a boy, on the left), Leah (a girl, in the middle) and Siti (a girl holding a book, on the right). Panel 1. Vincent: As part of our Values-in-Action project, let's fold 1000 paper cranes to bring cheer to the residents of Joy Elderly Home! Leah: Great idea, Vincent! Since all of us have folded paper cranes before, we should be able to finish them quickly. I'm sure the residents will love the colourful display. Let's call it "Paper Project Crane" or "Bring a Smile". Siti: Leah, I prefer the latter. We'll need tape, coloured paper and nylon string to make and hang the cranes. Panel 2. Vincent: The leftover tape from our last project should be enough. I'll email Mrs Wong to help us get the rest of the items by 31 August. Leah: Perhaps, we should also share how our class plans to interact with the elderly. Siti: I agree! We should get the items by 20 August to give ourselves ample time to fold the cranes.

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Purpose: to propose the project ideas to Mrs Wong and ask for her help to get the items. Say this in the opening lines.
Audience and tone: Mrs Wong is your form teacher, so the email is formal and polite. Begin 'Dear Mrs Wong', use no slang or short forms like 'gonna', and thank her at the end.
Context: you are Vincent, writing after the discussion with Leah and Siti on 17 August 2026. Write as 'I' and 'we', and sign off as Vincent with your class.

Point 1, name and objective: the project is called "Bring a Smile". Siti preferred 'the latter', which means the second of the two names, so it is not "Paper Project Crane". The objective is to bring cheer to the residents of Joy Elderly Home.

Point 2, how the activity was decided: the class chose to fold 1000 paper cranes because all of them have folded paper cranes before, so they should be able to finish quickly (and the residents will love the colourful display).

Point 3, items and date: the items to be purchased are coloured paper and nylon string. Do not ask for tape, because the leftover tape from the last project should be enough. Ask to have the items by 20 August, to give the class ample time to fold the cranes. Vincent first said 31 August, but Siti then suggested 20 August and gave the reason.

Point 4, your own information: give one sensible way the class will interact with the elderly, for example teaching the residents to fold a crane, chatting with them while hanging up the cranes, or singing songs for them.

Format and language: a short subject line, greeting, clear paragraphs, a polite closing request and sign-off. Write in complete sentences and check tenses, spelling and punctuation. Marks: 6 for task fulfilment, 8 for language and organisation.

questions.stem:
Part 2: Continuous Writing
Write a composition of ++at least 150 words++ about **something precious.**
The pictures are provided to help you think about this topic.
Your composition must be based on at least one of these pictures.
[[img1]]
Consider the following points when you plan your composition:
• What was precious?
• Why was it precious?
You may use the points in any order and include other relevant points as well.

images.alt: Three pictures, one below the other. Picture 1: a wristwatch showing about four o'clock. Picture 2: a boy and a girl in school uniform smiling and talking with an elderly woman with glasses who is sitting in a wheelchair; the girl is holding the woman's hands. Picture 3: a folded greeting card standing up, with a sunflower drawn on the front.

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Understand the topic: 'something precious' is something of great value to you. It need not cost much. It can be an object, a person, time, a memory or a friendship. Your story must show clearly what was precious and why.

Picture 1 (watch): a watch that is a gift or a keepsake from a loved one, which is lost, broken or almost given up; or the watch can stand for time, such as precious time spent with someone before they move away.

Picture 2 (pupils with an elderly woman): precious time or a bond with a grandparent or a resident of a home; the precious stories and advice she shares; realising that her company matters more than games or gadgets.
Picture 3 (card with a sunflower): a handmade card from a friend, parent or teacher that is kept for years because of the words inside or the moment it was given.

Plan a story arc: introduction (set the scene and the precious thing), build-up (why it matters), problem (it is lost, damaged, taken for granted, or time is running out), climax (what the character does and feels), resolution.
Show why it is precious through actions, thoughts and feelings, not just by saying 'it was precious to me'.

End by returning to the topic: what the character learnt about what is truly precious. Use at least one picture, write at least 150 words, and check paragraphing, tenses and vocabulary. Marks: 18 for content, 18 for language and organisation.
